newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-PARLIAMENT TO CONSIDER INVESTMENT FUND LAW.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-PARLIAMENT TO CONSIDER INVESTMENT FUND LAW.

text.p: The parliament finance and budget committee has approved a new law on investment funds for its first reading and MPs hope to do the reading by the end of the current spring session.
"The parliament agreed this draft is urgent and should be included for the first reading in its last sittings of the spring session in June," Alfreds Chepanis, the parliament chairman, told Reuters.
"We could review the law in the second reading at the very beginning of the autumn session on September 4," he added.

Under the law, investment funds will be allowed to function for the first time. The funds will be supervised by the securities commission and the law regulates their activity, including setting the limits for the diversification of risks.
The law is expected to come into effect in twelve months after the parliament passes it for the sector to adjust to the new requirements.
The basic capital requirement for a fund will be 100,000 lats and own capital should be two thirds of the paid capital.

"The law will introduce a new form of security to the Latvian market, namely investment certificates," said Aivars Bernans of the economy ministry privatisation department, one of the authors of the draft.
The current version of the draft refers to open-end funds with the securities commission working on closed-end funds.
"The necessary amendments for closed-end funds to be included will be worked out by the (finance and budget commission) for the second reading," Bernans said.
"The risk diversification limit might differ for open-end and closed-end funds, the latter not having such high demands for being liquid," Bernans added.
